title: Add Labels/Tags and Status
body: Adding the deadline feature is great. But I want to make it more helpful. You can make it into a Status form where we can select "Not Started", "In Progress", or "Completed". Because sometimes I do a task on a certain day, but I don't really complete the whole thing yet. Also, you can add Tags/Labels in Google Tasks too so that we can filter them or categorize them if we want. That way, when there is a board view, we can see which tasks are needed for a certain category. These are inspired by Notion.

title: Simple app but lacks a lot of features to make it a daily driver
body:
First off, this app is wonderful. I love how simple it is but Google needs to work on it more if they want users to come from other apps such as Todoist.

Even if they are only aiming for a simple todo app, they are lacking in a lot of functionality to make it a daily driver.

One example is the inefficient use of space in the iPad. If you don’t have one, the iPad app is literally just the iPhone app but in a bigger screen. As in, the button placement is the same, you don’t have a sidebar (you technically have but it’s not always present like it should on a screen as big as an iPad), and other stuff.

Also, it lacks other stuff you can expect from a digital todo list. For example: a lack of a “Today” tab.

This is so dead simple to implement and every todo app should have that tab. Otherwise, they are just a grocery list app.

Another example is the lack of collaboration. You can’t share a list with other people so say goodbye to using this as an app if you work with other people.

While I don’t expect this to be a project management app, it still frustrates me you can’t let your roommate or something access your grocery list. Or if you are doing a group project, you can’t let someone else see the queued tasks.

Lastly, I believe this app lacks the thing that makes people switch from other apps: Integration with the Google Ecosystem.

You can’t use it with Google Docs. If you want to remind yourself to edit this part of the paper, you’d have to go to the Reminders app itself to do so. If you want to see your Google Tasks on Google Calendar, you’d have to disable Reminders first. If you want to link it to a Google Keep note, tough luck. You can’t.

This app has so much potential. I really hope Google can give it the priority. If it does, it might just become the daily driver of millions of people.
